All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

We keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 upcoming players, but did not upgrade two of the most vital positions on the pitch.

Industry observers note that only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the big difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Recent findings suggest that zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, rolled out a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

According to recent reports, spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a major mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

Industry observers note that “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

In a recent development, that sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he stated: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

It has been revealed that it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Jackson was not the only Villa upcoming boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

“They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery remarked. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

Recent findings suggest that “Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

Recent findings suggest that “Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig.

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:.

vs Man Utd (A) - Oct 10th, 5.30pm.

vs Coventry (H) - Oct 19th, 8pm.

vs Chelsea (A) - Oct 24th, 5.30pm.

vs Crystal Palace (H) - Oct 31st, 5.30pm.

vs Brentford (H) - Oct 10th, 3pm.

vs Fenerbahce (H) - Oct 14th, 8pm.

vs Newcastle (A) - Oct 17th, 5.30pm.

vs Man City (H) - Oct 24th, 12.30pm.

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia indicates his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD.

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Possession: Spurs 64% vs 36% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 31 vs 18.

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

Recent findings suggest that “We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we revealed a really good character.”.

And that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

Recent findings suggest that late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

It has been revealed that this will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

Another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

Recent findings suggest that callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

Sources indicate that though Savio takes the corner rapidly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

Maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

Recent findings suggest that kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

But it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

According to recent reports, A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

It looks like a Cash own goal...

Sources indicate that the Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye.

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher.

This is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

According to recent reports, this is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

Gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

The Spurs fans are flooding out.

Industry observers note that villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

In a recent development, gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

In a recent development, marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

Tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

Savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his fresh club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

Sources indicate that he gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Tonali sends a ball across to Savio on the right corner of the box, and his low ball in goes out the back for a corner.

Solanke can’t control it as it comes in and that will be his last action before he makes way for Maddison.

Marmoush goes down on the edge of the box, pushed by Joao Gomes, earning a free kick.

Robertson and Marmoush standing over it, just on the left of the area. Robertson is the one to take, lifting it towards the back post but Suzuki comes out to claim easily.

In a recent development, so close for Spurs! A fantastic run from Robertson but the defender strays just offside just outside the box. He takes the ball down to the back line, drawing Suzuki off his line, and it is crossed back past the keeper and bundled over the line by Kudus.

It has been revealed that huge cheers before VAR takes a look. The wait goes on.

Ruggeri intercepts a loose ball in midfield and makes a run down the left side. He lifts a ball towards the centre of the box, but Betancur beats the waiting Manzambi to it, bringing it down and nudging it towards his keeper.

Savio again on the right edge of the box lifts a ball across the box towards the back post, but Suzuki judges it well and comes off his line to claim it.

We’re back underway as Kinsky had to receive a bit of treatment there.

Recent findings suggest that tonali plays it in for Savio but it’s intercepted by a Villa shirt. It’s played out for Jackson on the left wing to have a run and he gets past van Hecke very easily to reach the edge of the area and take a shot – which goes high and wide.

Unai Emery warned Nicolas Jackson about getting unnecessary bookings yesterday after having to substitute him on a yellow card at half-time last week. 30 seconds into the second half, Jackson got a needless yellow car for stopping a free-kick being quickly taken. Emery pointed straight to his head when it happened.

Savio tries to find Bentancur as he makes a run down the centre of the field. The midfielder gets a head on it but it heads the wrong way.

In a recent development, but the game is opening as Spurs push, and Villa go on the counter with Manzambi running down the left side. He feeds a ball through to Jackson who carries it into the box but Kinsky judges it well and comes out to block the shot.

Spurs are pressing very high now and Villa have dropped very deep, especially their midfield.

Sources indicate that savio tries to put a ball in to the box but it’s trapped by Manzambi who plays the ball out. Ruggeri gets the ball back in to midfield to Buendia, who tees up Manzambi for a run into the box. The Swiss international is closed down well though.

Time to see how Spurs will react after that goal.

There’s still plenty of fight left as Kudus sends the ball out to Savio, trying to get to the touchline to cross a ball back in but Ruggeri stays on him.

We’re back in action in north London.

Spurs: Mateus Fernandes for Mohammed Kudus.

Villa: Wan-Bissaka for Matty Cash.

It has been revealed that and as I’m typing this , it’s an early yellow for Jackson for a silly foul. Here we go!

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

In a recent development, it looks like Mohammed Kudus will be on at half-time for football. He’s been going through his own half-time warm-up. Matt Cash has been doing the same for Villa, so maybe we will see him too.

Possession: Spurs 57% vs 44% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 14 vs 11.

Good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side presently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

But before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Middlesbrough have a number of key players, with Aidan Morris being one already linked with a January transfer window move away from The Riverside to join Bundesliga side VfB Stuttgart.

Will Lankshear's goals, Amario Cozier-Duberry's dribbling and creativity, and Adilson Malanda's composure may all catch the eye; but Aidan Morris has arguably been the heartbeat of this Middlesbrough side.

Kim Hellberg won't want to lose any of his best players in January, but Morris being linked with a move to Stuttgart from Middlesbrough could be a concern, per a recent report from German outlet BILD.

According to recent reports, FLW's Middlesbrough fan pundit Liam Day was asked about the fact Stuttgart are reportedly eyeing a move for Morris. We asked if this is hardly a surprise, is it? But also what price-tag would he place on the midfielder’s head right now and if he should be retained at all costs.

He replied: "I think simply because January, you know, you're in the midst of a promotion battle, you don't sell your stars.

"And I don't think there is any way he leaves; he seems very loyal to Boro, which is very nice.

"So, I think you've got to do all you can to try and retain him.

"But say Boro were to sell him, I think an offer of £30m-35m probably will do it.

Industry observers note that what would your valuation of Aidan Morris be? Comment below!

"He is a great player, no doubt about it, but that sort of money in the Championship is hard to say no to.

"Because you can then improve your overall squad, but I don't think you can get another Aidan Morris.

Industry observers note that "I think that's impossible. The covering of ground he does, his strength, his passing — it's all pretty ridiculous, in my opinion.

"So, you do have to try and retain him at all costs, but an offer of £30-35 million will probably do it.".

With Hayden Hackney joining Everton for an initial £16.5 million, rising to £24 million, as reported by Sky Sports, Morris’ superior off-ball quality, defensive control, and relentless pressing, justify a £25 million valuation at minimum.

Unlike Hackney’s box-to-box roaming to use his passing, Morris dictates tempo while shielding the backline, making him the more complete midfielder overall at Championship level.

Born in Florida, Morris developed through the Columbus Crew academy and Indiana University before signing professionally in 2020. After winning two MLS Cups and earning USMNT caps, Middlesbrough signed him for around $4 million (£3.1 million) in June 2024 (The Athletic).

Under Michael Carrick, Morris quickly became Boro's midfield engine. Now under Hellberg, his bravery on the ball and intelligence off it has elevated him into the club's undisputed focal point and standout player following Hackney’s departure.

It's no surprise that top clubs are looking at Morris and his Middlesbrough performances. He is someone Middlesbrough should be doing everything possible to keep hold of, but the same should apply to every other notable member of the squad.

Boro are in an excellent position heading into January and the last thing they need is to weaken their promotion prospects by allowing key players to leave. Instead, they should be looking to strengthen, particularly at left-back.

While potentially adding another striker to provide competition and support for Will Lankshear also would not hurt, with such a strong opportunity to challenge for promotion from the Championship.

Although clubs without parachute payments need to sell their best assets eventually, retaining the core of Hellberg's Middlesbrough squad is absolutely vital. January should be about adding quality, not subtracting it.

Lionesses and Arsenal star Chloe Kelly stole the show at the GQ Men of the Year Awards on Tuesday night, going braless in a see-through dress just hours after missing out on Sarina Wiegman's latest England squad.

The two-time Euros and Champions League winner arrived on the red carpet in a long-flowing navy dress, showing off her toned body and glamorous long blonde hair. She was joined by former England stars Mary Earps and Alex Scott.

Kelly was once again left out of Wiegman's selection for the play-offs against Ukraine due to a hamstring injury, as the winger's battle to make the plane for next summer's World Cup continues.

Wiegman revealed her squad on Tuesday morning, turning to England's younger generation for the double-header against Ukraine.

Izzy Goodwin is the latest emerging talent to receive a call-up to the Lionesses squad, after Lexi Potter, Erica Meg Parkinson and Freya Godfrey won their first caps in the previous round against Greece.

The 23-year-old London City Lionesses striker scored the equaliser against Kelly's Arsenal last weekend at the Emirates, with the home side dropping points yet again.

Chloe Kelly looked glamorous in a long-flowing navy dress at GQ Men of the Year 2026.

The 27-year-old missed out on Wiegman's England squad for the second time in a row.

Arsenal have had an underwhelming start to the season, with just three wins in 10 games, and they currently sit in sixth place in the WSL table.

Kelly was dropped for the first time by Wiegman for the previous qualifiers against Greece, alongside fellow forward Ella Toone.

'The main reason is that I think the levels weren't what I expect from them on the pitch,' Wiegman explained at the time.

Toone has returned to the latest squad, with Wiegman praising her reaction to being dropped last time out.

Industry observers note that 'She responded really well (to being dropped last camp),' Wiegman said: 'Working really hard, she came in and was ready straight away. Going back to club she's done well and that's what has been fed back to me, too.'.

Mark Noble has called on West Ham United supporters to help transform the London Stadium into an intimidating venue as Scott Parker prepares for his first home match in charge against Preston North End.

Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Noble praised the ‘extraordinary’ loyalty of West Ham fans following relegation and insisted that the club’s ambition remains an immediate return to the Premier League.

He also challenged supporters to make life uncomfortable for visiting teams, arguing that a crowd of 60,000 should give West Ham a significant advantage. But I think it’s key to point out that getting the fans onside and creating an intimidating atmosphere are probably two very different things.

There’s no doubt about it. When the London Stadium is loud, it is impressive, as anybody who attended that incredible night against Sevilla will testify.

But I do think it’s a long way from being intimidating.

For that to happen, I firmly believe supporters need to be close to the pitch.

Not just to cause opposition players discomfort, but to put pressure on referees and give West Ham the kind of home advantage that seems prevalent throughout the league.

The distance between the stands and the playing surface remains a fundamental problem, regardless of how many supporters are in attendance.

It’s something I’ve previously argued when discussing proposals to improve the stadium atmosphere.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium.

According to recent reports, it was always my concern that relegation to the Championship would see visiting teams regard a trip to the London Stadium as a lovely day out in opulent surroundings. Opposition changing rooms are grand and palatial and their team coach can pull into the venue untroubled by home fans.

Industry observers note that and our results in Stratford have certainly done little to disprove that theory. However, that doesn’t mean things can’t improve.

I genuinely believe that getting West Ham playing on the front foot will help eliminate some of the eerie silences we’ve heard so frequently at the London Stadium.

Noble wants supporters to see a team giving everything, and I think he’s absolutely right about that.

If Parker can produce an aggressive, attacking side that gives the crowd something to get excited about, the atmosphere should improve considerably.

But turning the London Stadium into a genuinely intimidating venue is another matter entirely.

And unfortunately, that’s a problem which can’t be solved simply by asking 60,000 people to make more noise.

  • The ownership of Blackburn Rovers by the Indian chicken magnates Venky's has seldom been uncontroversial, but an interview with one of the club's former managers has now shone light on the circumstances surrounding his departure from Ewood Park, and even though this happened more than a decade ago, it doesn't paint a particularly flattering picture of the owners.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The former Blackburn Rovers manager Paul Lambert has explained the circumstances which surrounded his departure from the club at the end of the 2015-16 season, and it doesn't shine a positive light on the owners.

The ownership of Blackburn Rovers by the Indian chicken magnates Venky's has seldom been uncontroversial, but an interview with one of the club's former managers has now shone light on the circumstances surrounding his departure from Ewood Park, and even though this happened more than a decade ago, it doesn't paint a particularly flattering picture of the owners.

In a recent development, paul Lambert joined Blackburn as a replacement for Gary Bowyer following Bowyer's dismissal in November 2015, which came with the team in 15th place in the Championship table. But Lambert didn't last very long in the position, leaving the club at the end of the season after activating a release clause in his contract.

Little more information over what had actually happened was revealed at the time, but the interview fills in the gaps and reveals that it was the result of a dispute over the sale of striker Jordan Rhodes that resulted in the manager leaving after spending just eight months at Ewood Park.

As reported by the Blackburn Telegraph, the former Blackburn Rovers manager has confirmed that he left Rovers at the end of the 2015-16 season following a dispute over what happened to the proceeds of the sale of striker Jordan Rhodes.

Lambert explained: "We thought we were going to get a bit of a war chest to crack on for the following season, because the remit was to keep Blackburn in the league and then rebuild. We went in there and were doing pretty well, and then around November time, I got told we had to sell Jordan Rhodes. I thought, ‘Well, he is our best striker, he scores the goals for us.’".

The manager confirmed that he asked about what would happen with the proceeds of this sale, and was told that it would be spent on squad-building: "So I stated, ‘Where does the money go?’ And they went, ‘Well, it will come back to you.’ It never came back.".

In a recent development, should Blackburn have kept hold of Jordan Rhodes in January 2016? Let us know your views in the comments below!

Lambert didn't get the answer that he was expecting from the club about the funds from the sale when it completed, either: "Around February I went to see one of the guys and stated, ‘Listen, I am going to leave now because this isn't going to work.’".

Lambert mentioned that he was talked around to staying until the end of the season by this member of the club's senior management: "He said, ‘Please, Paul, stay until the end of the season.’ I thought we'd have got money to kick on, but there was never any money coming.".

The picture that he painted of the club at that time wasn't flattering in the slightest: "I didn't want to put myself through that, and I wasn't enjoying it anyway. There was no enjoyment in it. Things were not getting done, there was no investment coming in, players were getting sold, and there was so much going on behind the scenes that I thought I may as well leave.".

The position regarding Jordan Rhodes by the time of the January transfer window was complex. The striker had been a record club signing when he arrived from Huddersfield Town in August 2012, costing them £8 million. But by the summer of 2015, Rhodes was a wanted man, and Middlesbrough made a bid for him described as being "in excess of £10 million", which left the striker unhappy.

Speaking to ESPN after the rejection of the offer, Rhodes remarked: "When I left Huddersfield I felt the timing was right in the next stage of my career and, having seen Middlesbrough's performances last season in reaching the playoff final and their ambition this summer in terms of acquisitions, I would have liked to have been able to talk to them and I am unhappy at not being given that opportunity.".

By the time that Lambert arrived at Ewood Park, then, the fact that Rhodes was coveted by other clubs and wanted to leave Ewood Park was common knowledge. But the fact that his eventual sale to Middlesbrough wasn't tied up until the very, very end of the following January's transfer window meant that there was no time to bring in a straight swap replacement. Rovers had quite a busy January transfer window, but they certainly didn't spend the millions that Lambert believed he was told would be made available.

In a recent development, blackburn Rovers were in 15th place in the Championship at the point of Paul Lambert's appointment, and they finished the season in exactly the same position in the table. He was replaced in the summer by Owen Coyle, but he only lasted until February 2017, by which time Rovers were in serious trouble near the bottom of the table.

It has been revealed that tony Mowbray was appointed as his replacement, but the club were still relegated at the end of the 2016-17 season. Whether they were better off with or without Paul Lambert is something of a moot point, but Blackburn certainly paid a price for losing the goals of Jordan Rhodes.

Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

He needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

Industry observers note that when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Recent findings suggest that since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Sources indicate that don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Sources indicate that isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

Industry observers note that one, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

“Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose stated. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that demonstrated why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

Industry observers note that his first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

It has been revealed that everything Iraola has remarked and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

Sources indicate that there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has noted that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he mentioned: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

Sources indicate that “We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He mentioned: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his major move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Industry observers note that liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

Recent findings suggest that the Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

What Nigel Pearson told Jamie Vardy after shock Leicester City exit request

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jamie Vardy has revealed how a conversation with Nigel Pearson helped change the course of his iconic spell at Leicester City shortly after joining from Fleetwood Town in 2012.

Vardy's career story is one of the most talked about in English football, and it is one which very few other names in the game have been able to replicate since.

The Sheffield-born native enjoyed strong success in the latter stages of his career after biding his time in the non-league game with the likes of Stocksbridge Park Steels, FC Halifax Town and, of course, the Cod Army.

With Pearson beginning the first full season of his second spell at Leicester in 2012, the experienced manager broke the non-league transfer record for an outgoing player when Vardy signed for £1m after having netted 34 goals for the Lancashire side as they won the Conference title.

What Vardy and the Foxes went on to achieve individually and collectively was unprecedented, but it wasn't always plain sailing for the striker in the East Midlands.

Vardy's first season at the King Power Stadium saw Leicester finish sixth, losing to Watford in one of the most iconic EFL games of all-time in the Championship play-off semi-finals.

However, the forward scored just four times in 26 regular-season appearances - 17 of which were starts due to competition with the likes of Chris Wood, David Nugent and Harry Kane, on loan from Tottenham Hotspur at the time.

Asked by fellow former striker, Emile Heskey, on how he sees his legacy in LE2, Vardy revealed his early struggles with the club and how Pearson blocked a potential exit.

Industry observers note that "It was so hard, I'll be honest," stated the 39-year-old. "I think, because I'd not done the academy route, it was working out exactly what I needed to do.

"What was good enough when I was at Stocksbridge and Halifax wasn't what I needed to be doing at Fleetwood, for instance, and then what I did there was totally different from what was to come.

Recent findings suggest that "I was just eating 'crap', which is what I did previously and it worked. But, you get found out and there's a lot you have to change," Vardy added.

Industry observers note that "That first season was a struggle, but when you start to realise what you need to do. The summer after the first season, I went on holiday, but my holiday's not just a holiday, I'm running in the streets, making sure I'm fit when I get back.

Leicester fans, what are your recollections of Jamie Vardy's initial struggles for form? Comment below!

"That first season was a massive struggle, but when it clicked the second year, it was like 'I am meant to be here'," he continued.

"I fully doubted myself. I remember saying to Nigel Pearson and Craig Shakespeare, 'send me back to Fleetwood. I know I can score goals there.

"They stated 'it's not happening', we've bought you for a reason. Knuckle down. Keep going. It's a good thing they did say that.".

Ultimately, Pearson and Shakespeare made the right call, as after a 16-goal season during the Foxes' 2013/14 Championship-winning season, Vardy went on an unbelievable run of goalscoring exploits.

In November 2015, the forward broke the record for the most goals in consecutive Premier League games - 11 - which helped Pearson's successor, Claudio Ranieri, oversee City's 5000-1 top-flight triumph, with Vardy netting 24 times that campaign.

Five years later, he won the Premier League's Golden Boot with 23 goals, and as well as winning the 2021 FA Cup and Community Shield with the club, stuck around to help Leicester win the 2023/24 Championship title, before departing last summer after an overall record of 200 goals in 500 appearances in blue.

Vardy spent last season with Cremonese in Serie A, but after his summer departure came intense speculation over a return to Leicester or a move to boyhood club, Sheffield Wednesday, following David Storch's takeover.

Neither would materialise, but in September, the former England international agreed a contract with Burnley until the end of the season, although his current Championship spell isn't going well at all for the Clarets.

Vardy arrived just weeks before Nicky Hayen's dismissal in East Lancashire, which came after he netted his first goal in the 2-1 home loss to Wolves on October 16th, whilst Fabio Celestini's reign has got off to a winless start ahead of Sunday's grudge match against Blackburn Rovers.

Results will dictate how things play out, but Saints have put things in place for Eckert to lead them to what they will hope is a successful era.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leon Scarlett is already attracting the attention of some of Europe's biggest clubs as a result of his appearances for the Wales under-21 team, and this puts pressure on his current club to tie him down to a professional contract.

One of the more notable downsides of the information age is that when a football club unearths a rare gem, it won't be very long before the game's apex predators find out about them as well. With every game now recorded and scrutinised, it's seldom long before news of an emerging talent will land with them, and they will be likely to take an interest in the player concerned before they become prohibitively expensive.

In the case of the 17-year-old winger Leon Scarlett, Queens Park Rangers might have a star of the future on their hands. Scarlett has only made six appearances for Rangers, of which five have been as a substitute, and he has yet to record his first goal or assist in a Rangers shirt, but such is his already growing reputation that some significant names, including Arsenal, AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt have already been connected with an interest in him, among a rapidly growing list of clubs.

In a tight Championship table, Queens Park Rangers have acquitted themselves well in 2026-27 and look capable of battling for promotion this term.

But while Rangers fans can get excited about the possibility of a serious bid for a play-off place or beyond following years of stagnation in the table, it's the attention being lavished upon Leon Scarlett which gives them cause to be the most excited, but in all likelihood also a little nervous over the possibility of losing him.

According to recent reports, how far do you think Leon Scarlett could go in his professional career? Let us know in the comments below!

Sources indicate that scarlett, who can play on either the left or the right wing, originally joined QPR's academy following his free transfer arrival from Arsenal in April 2025, and made his debut for them from the bench in their 3-0 loss at Ipswich Town at the very end of the 2025-26 season. So far this season, he's made a further five appearances in a hooped shirt, including a full debut for them against Preston North End in September, although he was withdrawn at half-time in this match.

Recent findings suggest that but QPR aren't the only team for whom he's been playing. Although still only 17-years-old, and having already played for their under-16 and under-17 teams, he made two brief appearances for the Wales under-21 team against Belgium and Austria at the end of September, while he also completed three appearances for the under-19 team during the November international break which included providing an assist in their 2-2 draw with Iceland in a play-off match for the Under-19 Euros which they won on penalty kicks.

These tastes of international football have grown the young winger's profile. At the end of last week, Anthony Joseph of Sky Sports reported that both AC Milan and Eintracht Frankfurt are keeping tabs on him, while it's also been reported that Brighton, Rangers and even his former club Arsenal could be plotting a move for him. And the pressure on Rangers over Scarlett could be all the greater for knowing that the winger hasn't yet signed his first full professional contract with the Loftus Road club.

Recent findings suggest that both the Queens Park Rangers club captain Jimmy Dunne and manager Julien Stephan are clear admirers of Leon Scarlett. As reported by Loft For Words in September, Dunne spoke about the teenager at a fans forum in glowing terms, saying: "Just watching Leon Scarlett today he’s so impressive, so bright, and so positive. You want to see him do well and thrive. We’ve got loads of exciting players like that. I was here at the U21 game the other day and they were fabulous.".

Recent findings suggest that julien Stephan also praised him at this forum, saying: "Why in the last two games did I pick Leon Scarlett? Because he deserves it. He highlighted in all the training sessions it was the right moment for him. Never a coincidence. Always logical.".

In April, as reported by the Evening Standard, Stephan had previously remarked of Scarlett: "The last game (Scarlett) did for the U21s, he did very well. I saw him in a cup game with the U18s earlier in the season, and he did a good first half. So I just wanted to see him during the session with us (the first team). And during the session, he did well.” Scarlett earned his senior debut shortly after this.

There is one thing that Queens Park Rangers can do to try and secure their position regarding this young talent. Scarlett remains on a scholarship with the club and hasn't yet signed his first full professional contract with them. Rangers should surely try to tie him down to a senior contract, which would mean that, in the event that he continues to show the promise that he has so far and clubs remain interested in snatching him from them, they would be able to land a substantial transfer fee for him.

This could, of course, end in disappointment. Scarlett has the right to say no to any offer made to him, and any refusal to agree terms with Rangers would surely be a precursor to him leaving the club. But as things stand, the club would have next to no chance of keeping hold of him, and with the list of clubs who are tracking him continuing to grow, Queens Park Rangers might be best advised to do everything within their power to keep this exciting young prospect at their club for as long as possible. Judging by his comments in September, it would certainly make Jimmy Dunne happy.

Manchester United parted ways with Michael Carrick after a disastrous start to the Premier League season with just one win from 10 games.

Manchester United have spent a reported 12 million to bring Mauricio Pochettino and his coaching team from the United States to Old Trafford, with the Argentine determined to work alongside several familiar faces.

United paid around $10 million to secure Pochettino’s release from the US team and with a further $2 million reportedly required to secure members of his backroom staff.

The 54-year-old has built a close working relationship with his coaching team throughout spells at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea. Several of those staff members have followed him to Manchester United.

Jesus Perez is Pochettino’s long-time assistant and is widely regarded as his right-hand man. Their relationship began at Espanyol, where Perez initially worked as an analyst before becoming his assistant at Southampton. He has followed the Argentine throughout his career with spells at Tottenham, PSG and USA. He is now set to take the same role at Old Trafford.

Jimenez will work as United’s goalkeeping coach. He first joined Pochettino’s coaching setup at Espanyol in 2011 and has remained alongside him throughout his managerial career, including their time in England, France and the United States.

Industry observers note that the manager’s 31-year-old son has also joined the coaching group. Sebastiano started working with his father during their time at Tottenham and has continued as a sports scientist and fitness coach with him with the USA team. He is also joining Pochettino at Manchester United.

Sources indicate that the former Argentine defender has worked with Pochettino since his first managerial job at Espanyol. He has been involved in training sessions, video analysis and tactical preparation, helping the manager develop game intends.

The arrivals mean a major change behind the scenes at Carrington following the departures of Michael Carrick and his coaching staff.

Mauricio Pochettino is set to face Liverpool in his first game as Manchester United head coach on Sunday.

#106943. Inside the 'uncomfortable' world of football documentaries: The shocking 'lack of respect' shown to managers, how Pep Guardiola learned to love the cameras - and why Mauricio Pochettino's appointment is bad news for Amazon's crew at Carrington

Inside the 'uncomfortable' world of football documentaries: The shocking 'lack of respect' shown to managers, how Pep Guardiola learned to love the cameras - and why Mauricio Pochettino's appointment is bad news for Amazon's crew at Carrington

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2123 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.

Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.

The club’s latest managers, a double act from nearby Ramsbottom United, stood behind the goal studying the Salford squad. Neville approached them at full time, asking if they’d like to say a few words inside the dressing room – or more accurately, portacabin – by way of introduction.

Sources indicate that ‘It was dark at full time,’ co-manager Anthony Johnson recalls. ‘I’m not exaggerating the point, I opened the door and there were these cameras, these lights on. Nobody told us about a documentary.

Sources indicate that 'The lights literally came on and I went, “S***, I’m under the spotlight here”. There was no training, nobody sits you down to tell you how it works.’.

First airing in a primetime slot on BBC One, Salford’s Class of ’92 docuseries was hooked on the Manchester United legends owning the club but swiftly became a show about the shouty personalities of Johnson and his partner, Bernard Morley, charting three promotions through non-League from 2015.

It has been revealed that salford are the smallest club ever to be the focus of this form of storytelling. Now, such documentaries are a popular vehicle for the country's elite.

Co-managers Anthony Johnson (left) and Bernard Morley became the accidental stars of a BBC documentary about the Class of 92's ownership of Salford City.

The celebrity of (from left) Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, Ryan Giggs and Phil Neville was juxtaposed with Salford's humble facilities on the series.

The Amazon cameras were in for Manchester City’s title-winning campaign in 2018 and also collaborated with the club to document the end of Pep Guardiola’s reign.

They are across town this year, right in the middle of United’s worst start to a season since the 1980s. Amid the infighting, public rows, Michael Carrick’s sacking and Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, the streaming service should emerge as the real victors of what has been an inconceivably dismal three months at Old Trafford.

The sight of a camera crew scuttling out of a press conference with Carrick weeks before he was relieved of his duties, boom mic hovering, painted a neat picture of the additional stress that can be placed upon managers when the pound signs prove too large for executives to ignore.

Recent findings suggest that ‘You can’t be yourself,’ states Simon Grayson, Sunderland manager at the start of their infamous Netflix drama Sunderland 'Til I Die, with part one culminating in relegation from the Championship in the 2017-18 season. ‘You never forgot the cameras are there.’.

It has been revealed that like Johnson, Grayson had been unaware of the planned documentary. David Moyes rejected the idea the year before when he was Sunderland boss, just as Ruben Amorim did at United in 2025.

Sources indicate that grayson didn’t grant Netflix access to ‘the inner sanctum’ and provided them footage of training remotely. Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has had the power to dictate where and when crews can film across their 57 episodes of Welcome to Wrexham.

Industry observers note that ‘I’m a private person,’ Grayson adds. ‘I don’t like people seeing what I’m doing. There were times when they actually tried to overstep the mark... you’d limit them to where the cameras would be.

'Even the players would say they were apprehensive and felt it was a bit intrusive. Aiden McGeady mentioned that he felt really uncomfortable doing it, as the rest of the dressing room did.’.

Vincent Kompany didn't like the way he was portrayed as a hot-head in a documentary during his time at Burnley.

Pep Guardiola relaxed his attitude towards the film-makers covering Man City when they learned where to position themselves in his dressing room without acting as a distraction.

Intriguingly, Guardiola embraced the cameras – but only eventually, initially insisting that filming could not resemble a circus. There was a scarcity of dressing room footage in Amazon’s 2018 edition. Only the notorious tirade at his players during half-time of a tempestuous FA Cup defeat at Wigan made it but that changed when City embedded their own production staff.

Sources say a relaxing of rules took time, around 12 months, as camera operators learned where to stand without acting as a distraction or finding themselves physically in the way.

Sources indicate that city have been part of five documentaries in six years now, with Guardiola so enamoured by the producers that they became part of the backroom staff – even acting as auxiliary kit men on away days. He sent personal audio messages of thanks when he bid farewell last May.

It has been revealed that he utilised them to create montages for pre-match speeches and leant on them to film players in slow motion to watch the gait of a player recovering from injury. That comes from the cameras being part of the furniture.

Critics will argue an in-house production is to the detriment of the eventual sanitised product, although City will point to Guardiola’s emotional breakdowns in A Beautiful Obsession – the story of his final season at City – as being raw and uncut.

In a recent development, the format is now moving towards in-season docs (regular episodes being available during a season rather than the whole show coming out at the end). This mirrors success stories in NFL and A Beautiful Obsession co-director John De Caux believes full-season pieces are ‘slightly on the wane’.

It has been revealed that ‘There were changes (in camera staff) all the time,’ Johnson says, reflecting on Salford’s annual series while he was in charge. ‘We were losing at half-time in one game… I make no apologies for this but I came in and went, “Move out of the f***ing way”. In previous seasons, they’d know not to be in that position.

Industry observers note that ‘You're having the same conversations again. It was like, "Hang on a minute. I've had this conversation before". The previous people knew about it. They have the footage from earlier seasons – so do your homework, like we all do with our jobs. It almost felt like a bit of a lack of respect at times.’.

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for an eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise cameras were rolling.

Former Sunderland boss Simon Grayson was unaware of their planned Netflix documentary and didn't grant the producers access to his inner sanctum.

These are the challenges that Amazon face with United, somehow attempting to earn trust or forging relationships in a matter of months before they pack up and leave. The film crew will be seen as outsiders.

There is intrigue within the industry as to exactly how granular Amazon can go amid the United chaos and whether they use fly-on-the-wall cameras, as was the case with Arsenal (in 2021–22) and Tottenham (in 2019-20).

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for that eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise the cameras were rolling.

According to recent reports, unlike Mourinho, Pochettino – his predecessor, sacked in November 2019 – had banned them from his office. He was never keen on the idea of the documentary and hardly features in the series, his dismissal coming early in Episode One – a sign perhaps that the film-makers got little out of him.

It will be fascinating to see if they gain access to his inner sanctum at United.

The club have had to double their media commitments this season as a result of the streaming deal, although they have been reluctant to organise sitdown interviews with players, telling Amazon that they must establish their own rapport for those.

Some clubs have been known to give their content away for free, with Sky Sports taking two seasons of Mission to Burnley without paying. The driving force behind those moves is to promote brands. Under Alan Pace’s premiership, Burnley are staring at potential relegation to League One.

Vincent Kompany, then the Burnley manager, is understood to have been vexed at his portrayal as a hot-headed screamer. Brendan Rodgers cannot have been overly pleased with Being: Liverpool, which ended in public ridicule and comparisons to David Brent. Players at other clubs have confided that they hid from cameras.

‘You can’t be yourself, you never forget the cameras are there,’ indicates Grayson of his season alongside the makers of Sunderland 'Til I Die.

Salford's co-manager Anthony Johnson gives his players a dressing down in the BBC documentary.

According to recent reports, joey Barton, meanwhile, is still waiting for his moment – and may be for some time. Fleetwood Town commissioned their own team to chart his start in management and streaming giants Dazn purchased the rights.

It was so close to being aired that Fleetwood held a premiere at Highbury Stadium for 100 supporters including the local mayor, only for one of Barton’s brushes with law enforcement in the intervening days to suspend the broadcast. Prolonged legal proceedings meant the idea was canned and Dazn’s licencing period expired.

It was later resurrected, focusing in part on then Fleetwood owner Andy Pilley’s fraud trial – a crew followed him into court on day one – but was then shelved when a guilty verdict was handed down. Cameras are following clubs up and down the EFL from Birmingham to Cambridge via Sheffield Wednesday.

Grayson, for his part, refused to share his drive home from training with the crew and now admits that the ultimately unfavourable edit may have been a result of him not giving the production organization what they wanted.

‘I did a presentation with the players with a flip chart and everybody thought it was an hour before kick-off of a league game,’ he states. ‘It was actually done at 11:30am before a pre-season game!

It has been revealed that 'That’s why I let them film it, because it was a pre-season game, and it had no real meaning. But they presented it in the doc as if it was before the first game of the season.

'Part of the severance when I was sacked was that I still needed to do some work for them. I did three different (choreographed) interviews in a London hotel with different shirts on after I’d been sacked, done as if they were filmed at the time.

Industry observers note that ‘People said, “You didn’t come across that passionate about the club when you were talking about it”. Well, why would you when you were filming in November after you’d already been sacked? We were talking about deadline day in one of them. I’d already done something on that in August.

Sources indicate that ‘I think they had sympathy with me, but also if they’d had more sympathy, they wouldn’t have even asked me to do it. I’ve spoken to managers since and they’ve gone, “F***ing hell, you did well to put up with that".'.

Grayson only ever watched four episodes back and has heard his successor, Chris Coleman, was also dealt a raw deal.

Fabian Delph leads a Manchester City inquest during an FA Cup defeat at Wigan - the only scene from the dressing room that made it into Amazon's documentary on the 2017-18 season.

In a recent development, mauricio Pochettino banned cameras from his office in his final days at Tottenham. Will he do the same at Manchester United?

Sources indicate that by his own admission, Johnson enjoyed the process more than Grayson did. One ex-Salford player claimed that nothing was really cut from the show other than a fight on a team-bonding night out. It was authentic, no-holds barred.

Until the end of Johnson and Morley, that is.

‘We won the league and we ended up getting sacked anyway,’ Johnson notes. ‘We went to meet Gary (Neville) and the board. We went upstairs in Hotel Football and a cameraman followed us. Obviously they knew what was going on. When we got to the room for the meeting, they wouldn't let the camera in.

‘I'm actually smiling thinking about it. The documentary followed me and Bern everywhere, eating food or whatever, and then when the day comes to sack us, they didn't want the camera in the room!

‘The conversation was fine in the room itself but I think the perception from the outside world looking in would've been: "What the f*** is that all about?”’.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Sources indicate that pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

As he faces Liverpool for his first game on Sunday, the question arises: is he facing the toughest job in the Premier League?

The question was posed on BBC Radio about who is going to have more pressure, Pochettino or Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

According to former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, the expectations surrounding Manchester United will make the Argentine’s job considerably harder.

Pochettino is preparing for his first game in charge of Manchester United, with Liverpool waiting at Anfield on November 22. However, the challenge facing the upcoming manager goes beyond getting results on the pitch.

Onuoha believes Pochettino will have to deal with constant discussion and criticism about his work, much of it coming from former United players who are now in the media.

Choosing between Pochettino and Frank, Onuoha said, “Probably Pochettino, because every former Manchester United player works in the media, so there will always be discussion around what he is doing.

In a recent development, “Whereas Frank can just enjoy playing his football at Crystal Palace. If he does well then it is great, if he doesn’t do well then it is still OK.

“But from Pochettino’s perspective, if Manchester United finish the season 15th in the Premier League, whether we like it or not, there will be some criticism of him because he’s had 28 games to do something.”.

The comments just highlight the difference in expectations at the two clubs. Frank may have more freedom to work without the same level of attention, while Pochettino will be judged from day one against the standards historically associated with Manchester United. That is one major problem for Pochettino.

Recent findings suggest that rory Smith from The Observer highlighted another glaring problem at United. Highlighting a major problem, Smith said, “there is a cycle element to Manchester United whereby a manager comes in, makes things a bit better, and then within a year to 18 months they aren’t challenging for titles again because the Premier League has changed since they were a dominant force.”.

In a recent development, pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. That opening fixture will give him an immediate test, but the bigger task will be to get back United to winning ways, step by step.

Will the Manchester United job be without pressure for Mauricio Pochettino? Absolutely Not.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wolves had an eventful summer after their embarrassing relegation from the Premier League last season, with Jordan James among the arrivals.

Many expected a huge turnover of players at Molineux, but whilst that didn’t happen, there was a refresh of the group, and Cesar Peixoto’s squad was boosted by some high-profile additions.

Bringing in Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez on free transfers caught the eye, and James was another arrival that was seen as a coup, as he was named Young Player of the Year in the Championship following his performances at Leicester last season.

Despite the Foxes’ struggles, James was outstanding, scoring 11 goals in 34 games for a side that were relegated to League One.

Dropping to the third tier meant James was not going to extend his stay at the King Power Stadium, so he returned to Rennes, and a summer of speculation followed.

There were plenty of links to Premier League clubs, with Fulham thought to be very keen, but it was ultimately Wolves who won the race for his signature.

Interestingly, James confirmed he had top flight offers, but he explained that he chose Wanderers as he didn’t want another year battling to stay up, having suffered relegations with Leicester and Birmingham in his relatively short career so far.

On that front, James’ move to Wolves has worked out, as Peixoto’s side are firmly in the hunt to win promotion, and there will be a belief in the group that they can not only go up, but fight for the title as well.

Yet, there’s no denying that James’ time at Wolves hasn’t gone as envisaged so far, as he has made just three starts from his 11 appearances in the league.

There have been flashes of his undoubted ability, including a superb goal against Stoke, but James has failed to establish himself as a key player under Peixoto.

To make matters worse, after making back-to-back starts for the first time under the Portuguese head coach, James was forced off after just 36 minutes with a hamstring concern against Cardiff at the end of October.

We know that the Championship is a marathon not a sprint, so there won’t be too many concerns about James’ lack of impact so far.

The 22-year-old will be hugely frustrated at the timing of his latest injury, but he will still expect to have a crucial role in Peixoto’s side over the course of the season.

It should be remarked that a disrupted pre-season meant James was starting behind the rest of his teammates, but, once he does get back up to speed, he will want to make a big impact.
